submission:
Root cause: The front-door service nginx-web-server stopped doing work while remaining reachable: across the full ~30-minute window spanning onset it emitted no access or error log lines [tr_b42ca415bd08] and not a single span [tr_77d8e6acee83], which is anomalous for an edge proxy that normally logs every request. No change landed between its creation burst and onset to explain a content-level regression [tr_71f8714f5626], and downstream compose-post-service is equally silent [tr_bdff52fbd51f] because nothing is being forwarded to it. Total silence from the alerting entry service with no error signal anywhere is the signature of a stopped process whose socket still accepts, leaving callers to hang to their deadlines. Confidence is low: every metric dispatch returned an unavailable series rather than a measurement [tr_28928cb4f5ae][tr_e44cb5f7f0bc][tr_5c01829f25f9], and both log queries used pod-name regexes that could themselves have missed the pods.
Faulty component: nginx-web-server
Fault type: process_freeze
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- A trace query scoped to nginx-web-server over the full incident window returned no traces at all, so the question of which downstream call carries the error or latency cannot be answered from trace data in this window. (found, from trace_query on nginx-web-server)
- The absence is total rather than partial: not a single span for the entry service was recorded, which is itself anomalous for a front-door service that would normally emit continuous traffic, and points either to a trace ingestion/sampling gap or to the service not serving requests during the window. (found, from trace_query on nginx-web-server)
- Traces will show the fault isolated to one downstream dependency (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, or user-timeline-service), letting us attribute the error status or latency to a specific call. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: With zero spans returned for the entry service, there are no parent-child relationships to inspect; none of the three candidate downstreams can be implicated or exonerated on trace evidence.)
- nginx-web-server is emitting traces normally and the problem is purely downstream latency visible in span durations. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: The query returned empty for the entry service itself, so the normal-emission premise fails; whatever is wrong includes or precedes the entry service's own telemetry.)
- The incident is a partial degradation affecting a fraction of requests that traces would let us sample and compare against healthy traces. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: A partial degradation would still leave successful traces in the window; the complete absence is inconsistent with a sampled-subset-degraded picture and suggests either full outage of the entry path or a telemetry pipeline break.)
- The investigation window was simply mis-scoped and traces exist just outside it. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: The query covered the full ~30-minute onset window as specified and returned nothing across its entirety, so a narrow off-by-a-few-minutes windowing error does not explain the result.)
- A Loki query for nginx frontend pods in the social-network namespace returned zero matching log lines across the full ~30-minute window spanning onset; no access lines and no error lines were retrieved, so no upstream names or upstream status codes could be observed. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The query targeted pods matching an nginx-thrift name pattern rather than a label for 'nginx-web-server' directly; a zero-match result is therefore consistent with either a genuine absence of logs or a selector/label mismatch, and the two cannot be distinguished from this result alone. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The result carries a truncation flag despite being empty, which is internally inconsistent and further weakens confidence that this query faithfully reflects the state of nginx logging during the window. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The nginx access/error logs will identify the failing upstream by name and show the upstream status codes driving the incident. (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: No lines were returned over the whole onset window, so this query yields no upstream names or upstream status codes; that attribution path is closed until the log source is retrieved by a different selector.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The incident can be characterised as an nginx-visible 5xx burst from a specific backend, evidenced in this window. (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: There is no nginx-side error or status evidence in this window at all, so no 5xx pattern can be established from nginx here.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- nginx was serving traffic normally and logging it throughout the window. (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: Even routine access logging produced no lines, so a 'normal, well-logged nginx' picture is not supported; either the pod was not serving/emitting, or its logs are not reaching this query path.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The only recorded changes for nginx-web-server in the window are three creation events by platform-automation about six minutes before onset: a ConfigMap and a Service (both upstream/routing definitions) created within a second of each other, followed by the workload container being created. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- The workload was created for the first time in this window, so the service entered the incident as a fresh deployment rather than a long-running instance that was mutated. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- No change landed between the creation burst and onset — there is a quiet gap of roughly six minutes with no configuration, deployment, or routing activity immediately preceding the failure. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- All three changes originate from the same automated actor, with no human or ad-hoc operator change recorded in the 24-hour window. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- A last-minute config edit or routing flip on nginx-web-server triggered the incident. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The change log for the service contains only initial creation records; no update, patch, or edit to the config or the upstream Service appears after creation or near onset.)
- A rollout or version bump of an existing nginx-web-server deployment regressed behaviour. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The container record is a first creation, not a replacement or redeploy, so there is no prior version for the current one to have regressed against.)
- The upstream definition was redefined or its endpoints repointed mid-window, breaking proxying. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The upstream ConfigMap and Service appear exactly once each, as creations, with no subsequent modification recorded in the window.)
- An unauthorised or manual operator change bypassed the normal pipeline. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: Every recorded change is attributed to the platform-automation actor; no separate human-initiated change is present.)
- The incident began on a stable, previously healthy instance, implying an environmental rather than provisioning cause. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The workload was created only minutes before onset, so there was no established steady state; misconfiguration present from first boot remains viable.)
- A Loki query for compose-post-service pods in the social-network namespace returned no log lines at all across the full 30-minute window spanning onset, so there is no recorded startup, readiness, or connection-failure output from this service in that period. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The absence is total rather than selective — no lines of any level matched the pod selector — which is more consistent with the service not emitting to Loki (not scheduled, not running, log shipping broken, or a pod-name pattern outside the regex) than with a quiet-but-healthy service, which would normally still emit periodic output. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The result is flagged as truncated, so the empty response should be treated as provisional pending a re-query with a broader selector before concluding the service produced nothing. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- compose-post-service logged an explicit crash, panic, or fatal error at onset that identifies the trigger (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: No log lines of any kind were returned for the service over the onset window, so no such message exists in Loki for this selector and time range.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- compose-post-service logged connection failures to a downstream dependency (database, cache, or another microservice), pointing the investigation at that dependency (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: The query covered all lines for the pods, not just errors, and returned nothing — no connection-failure evidence is available from this service's logs.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- compose-post-service was in a restart or crash-loop that would show repeated startup and readiness sequences in its logs (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: Repeated restarts would produce repeated startup output; the complete absence of lines means this cannot be confirmed from logs, and any such loop would have to be established from pod/restart-count data instead.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The service was running normally and logging routine request traffic throughout the incident (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: A healthy running service with log shipping intact would emit some output over 30 minutes; zero lines is inconsistent with normal operation plus working log collection.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The error-ratio metric query over the onset window returned no data at all, and the backend reported the failure as an instrumentation gap: this service emits no spans that are converted into Prometheus metrics, so span-derived error ratios are unavailable rather than measured-at-zero. (found, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server)
- No error rate, no status-code breakdown, and no upstream latency profile can be reported for nginx-web-server from span metrics for either the onset window or the preceding comparison window. (found, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server)
- The absence of errors in this metric view means nginx-web-server was healthy across onset and can be cleared as a suspect. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The backend explicitly distinguished unavailable from zero; the series does not exist for this service, so emptiness carries no health signal in either direction and the service remains unexcluded.)
- A status-code shift (e.g. a surge of 5xx versus 4xx) at the edge can be characterised from span-derived metrics in Prometheus. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: Status-code dimensions ride on the same span metrics that are absent for this service, so this data source cannot produce that breakdown at all; it must come from access logs or an nginx exporter instead.)
- Upstream latency degradation at the proxy can be confirmed or excluded from this query. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The same missing span pipeline carries upstream timing; no latency distribution exists here, so the query neither supports nor contradicts a latency hypothesis.)
- The query returned nothing because the chosen onset window was wrong or too narrow. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The failure is a service-level instrumentation gap reported independently of the window, and the baseline window is equally empty, so widening or shifting the window will not recover data.)
- The error-ratio metric query for compose-post-service returned no data at all over both the onset window and the preceding baseline window; the tool reported the query as failed rather than returning a zero or flat series. (found, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service)
- The stated cause of the empty result is an instrumentation gap: this error-ratio template is derived from span metrics, and the monitoring backend holds no span-derived metrics for this service because it does not emit traces that are converted into metrics. (found, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service)
- The absence is structural and not window-specific — it holds identically across the baseline period, so nothing about the onset window changed the availability of this series. (found, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service)
- compose-post-service received no request traffic during the onset window (silence on the metric means the service was idle or had stopped being called). (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service; why: The result is an explicit query failure due to missing span metrics, not a series of zero values. Traffic volume cannot be read from it in either direction.)
- compose-post-service is error-free / unaffected during the incident, since its error ratio shows nothing. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service; why: No error-ratio series exists for this service in the first place, so the result carries no information about its error behavior and cannot be read as a clean bill of health.)
- The empty series is a symptom of the incident — e.g. the service crashed, lost its scrape target, or its exporter went down at onset. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service; why: The same absence is present in the pre-incident baseline window, so it predates onset and is a standing instrumentation condition rather than an incident-induced change.)
- Retrying or widening this error-ratio query will surface the service's latency and error behavior. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on compose-post-service; why: The gap is in the data source itself — no span-derived metrics are stored for this service — so no choice of time range on this template will produce data.)

Reasoning:
The only positive observations are two total absences at the entry service: zero traces [tr_77d8e6acee83] and zero log lines [tr_b42ca415bd08]. The trace specialist noted the absence is total, not partial, which is inconsistent with a sampled, partially-degraded path. Metric emptiness carries no weight either way — all three metric dispatches failed as unavailable span-metric series, and the same gap exists in the pre-incident baseline, making it a standing instrumentation condition [tr_e44cb5f7f0bc][tr_28928cb4f5ae]. The change log rules out update, repoint, human edit, and redeploy on nginx, leaving only first-creation records and a quiet six-minute gap before onset [tr_71f8714f5626]. Among the hang-alike classes, a network_partition would normally leave the service's own log complaining it cannot reach upstreams, and disk_fill or bad_config would usually emit a diagnostic line; nginx wrote nothing at all. compose-post-service's silence [tr_bdff52fbd51f] follows from a frozen front door forwarding nothing, so no second fault is required.

Alternatives considered:
1. nginx-web-server: The nginx-thrift workload created six minutes before onset never started correctly, so the edge never served or logged anything. (bad_deploy). Ranked lower because: The change record shows a first creation with no prior version to regress from and no failed-create, restart, or retry entries [tr_71f8714f5626]; onset followed a quiet six-minute gap rather than coinciding with creation. Viable only because pod status was never read.
2. compose-post-service: compose-post-service stalled and nginx merely hung waiting on it, making the edge the service that noticed rather than the culprit. (dependency_latency). Ranked lower because: Zero spans and zero log lines exist for the entry service itself [tr_77d8e6acee83][tr_b42ca415bd08]; a proxy blocked on a slow backend would still log requests and timeouts. Nothing in the evidence implicates compose-post-service specifically [tr_ab2c2dafb187].

Open questions:
- Pod status and restart counts were never retrieved for nginx-thrift or compose-post-service; a crash-loop or never-ready pod looks identical to a freeze from these dispatches.
- Both Loki queries used pod-name regexes rather than a namespace label and returned an inconsistent truncation flag [tr_b42ca415bd08][tr_bdff52fbd51f], so the zero-match may be a selector miss rather than genuine silence.
- No caller-side evidence was gathered: whether clients hang to deadline or receive immediate errors is the distinction the verdict turns on, and it is unestablished.
